title: Do We Still Need Humans in the Loop? Human vs. LLM Annotation in Active Learning for TikTok Hate Speech Detection
abstract: arXiv:2604.13899v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Annotating data remains a costly bottleneck for supervised NLP. Active learning (AL) reduces the number of human labels needed by selecting only the most informative instances, while instruction-tuned LLMs attack the same bottleneck from the other side, making labels cheap enough to annotate entire corpora. This raises two questions: can LLM labels replace human labels within the AL loop, and does AL remain necessary when entire corpora can be cheaply labeled? We investigate both by training supervised hate speech classifiers on a new dataset of 278K German political TikTok comments, comparing human and LLM annotation under matched conditions. LLM annotation at scale outperforms human-supervised classifiers at roughly one-tenth the cost, for both a closed-source (GPT-5.2) and an open-weight (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B) LLM, and the advantage is robust under soft-label evaluation. translated_title: 我们还需要人在回路中吗？TikTok仇恨言论检测主动学习中的人工标注与大语言模型标注对比
translated_abstract: 数据标注仍然是监督式自然语言处理的一个昂贵瓶颈。主动学习（AL）通过仅选择最具信息量的实例来减少所需的人工标注数量，而指令微调的大语言模型（LLM）则从另一个角度攻克同一瓶颈，使标注成本足够低廉，能够标注整个语料库。这引出了两个问题：LLM标注能否在主动学习循环中取代人工标注？以及当整个语料库都可以被廉价标注时，主动学习是否仍然必要？我们通过在一个包含27.8万条德国政治TikTok评论的新数据集上训练监督式仇恨言论分类器来研究这两个问题，并在匹配条件下比较人工标注与LLM标注。结果显示，大规模LLM标注以约十分之一的成本超越了人工监督的分类器，无论是闭源模型（GPT-5.2）还是开放权重模型（Qwen3.5-122B-A10B）均是如此，且该优势在软标签评估下依然稳健。这一优势关键取决于标注界面：只有……
tldr: 在TikTok仇恨言论检测任务中，大规模LLM标注以约十分之一的成本超越了人工监督分类器，表明当LLM能廉价标注整个语料库时，主动学习中的人工标注环节可能不再必要。
en_tdlr: Large-scale LLM annotation outperforms human-supervised classifiers at roughly one-tenth the cost in TikTok hate speech detection, suggesting that human-in-the-loop active learning may no longer be necessary when LLMs can cheaply label entire corpora.
